Free AI video generators: what you get

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

Most “free” AI video tools give you a tight cap, a watermark, or both, and several $0 plans publish no clip count at all. Official pages were read Nov 15, 2026, 9:24–9:32 AM ET (6:24–6:32 AM PT). Google Flow still gives 50 credits a day, about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips at 720p if you spend every credit on Lite. Krea’s Free plan is 100 units a day with no credit card, from Krea's pricing page. Pika’s Free plan has no watermark and 0 monthly credits, from Pika's pricing page. Anything a vendor did not publish is marked unknown.

What do you actually get from a free AI video generator?

It varies widely, and several tools publish a $0 plan without publishing how many clips that plan can actually make. Google Flow gives 50 credits a day, which is about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips at 720p if you spend every credit on Lite. Krea gives 100 compute units a day with no card required, but does not publish a clip conversion on Free. Dreamina gives free daily credits (a Dreamina guide says 120 a day in the US). Runway gives 125 one-time credits. Pika’s Free plan includes all models and no watermark, but 0 monthly credits. Wan’s Free plan uses daily check-in credits whose amount is not published. Kling Basic, Higgsfield Free, and Hailuo Free also omit a usable clip count on the public pages we could read today.

    Which free AI video generator works with no sign-up?

    None of the official free video tiers we opened today publish a way to generate video with no account at all. The only plan that clearly says no credit card is required is Krea Free, which still requires you to sign up: the pricing page lists “Sign up for free” and “No credit card required” on the $0 plan with 100 units a day. Google Flow’s 50 daily credits are tied to a Google account (credits are shared across the account and are checked from your profile). Several other $0 plans offer sign-in or sign-up — Runway (“Start Free”), Pika (“START FREE” / Login), Dreamina (“Sign in”), Wan (“Log in to grab daily bonus”), Kling Basic (“Sign In to Claim Gift”), Higgsfield (Login / Get started, with a Free plan listed), and Hailuo (“Sign In,” and terms that welcome credits go to new registered accounts) — without saying whether a card is required to open the free tier. grok.com showed Sign in and Sign up next to a chat box; whether Grok video works without an account is unknown. x.ai/grok and meta.ai returned 403 in this check, so those remain unknown for no-account use. Luma still lists no public free plan. These sign-up and card facts were read Nov 16, 2026, 8:24 AM ET (5:24 AM PT).

    Which free option is best for each use?

    If you need a free AI video generator with no sign-up, none of the official tiers we checked today qualify. If you can create an account but do not want to enter a card, Krea Free is the only one that says “No credit card required.” For a repeating daily allowance you can count: Google Flow, at about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips a day if you use every credit on Lite, is the only row in this table with a published credits-per-clip figure. For a daily allowance without a card: Krea’s Free plan. For a watermark-free export on a $0 plan: Pika, which also includes all of its models, but only if you buy a credit pack or already have credits — Free itself includes 0 monthly credits and no commercial license. For a one-session trial of Runway’s tools: Runway’s 125 one-time credits. For Seedance in a consumer app with daily credits: Dreamina, with the US daily amount taken from a Dreamina guide, not from the plans table.

    What are the usual catches on a “free” plan?

    Watermarks are the most common: Hailuo Free downloads include one; Kling Basic, Wan Free, and Dreamina Free look likely to include one because watermark removal is listed as a paid benefit. Commercial use is often a paid-plan right — Pika Free, Kling Basic, and Higgsfield Free do not include it. Queues and caps: Higgsfield Free and Wan Free allow one generation at a time; Flow may block video for people without a paid plan around 2–5 PM UTC. Allotments can be one-time, not daily: Runway’s 125 credits do not refill, and Hailuo’s welcome credits expire after three days. Daily credits often do not roll over, as Flow’s help page states. A $0 plan with 0 monthly credits, such as Pika Free or Higgsfield Free, is not a source of recurring clips unless another grant is published.

    When does paying become cheaper per second?

    As soon as you need more clips than the free cap, a commercial license, or (on most tools except Pika) a watermark-free export, the free tier stops being a complete substitute. After that, the cheapest paid step is often not the vendor’s first consumer plan. In our catalog, a Krea yearly estimate for Veo 3.1 Lite at 720p is $0.0222/s, a Higgsfield yearly plan estimate for Kling 3.0 at 720p is $0.025/s, and the standard fal rate for MiniMax H3 Max Turbo at 480p is $0.025/s after the November 15, 2026 promo ended. Those figures assume you use the credits you pay for, and each row states its tier, resolution, and audio. A credit pack on a $0 plan can also cost more per clip than the first paid plan if the pack rate is worse; on Pika, packs and Starter are both listed at 60 credits per $1.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
